borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development would result in the loss of a family-sized dwellinghouse, the need for which is clearly demonstrated in the Development Plan and supporting evidence base. Furthermore, the applicant fails to accurately demonstrate that there is an identified need for the children's home and the type of care proposed, which would not meet the current needs of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham (LBBD) Children’s Social Care, as confirmed by LBBD's Lead Commissioner in Children's Social Care. As such, the proposal is considered to have a detrimental impact on the borough's supply of family housing, would fail to meet local need and is therefore contrary to the following policies: National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024) Policy D7, H1, H12 and S2 of the London Plan (March 2021) Policies SP3 and SPDG1 of the LBBD Local Plan  (September 2024)

The proposed dropped kerb is located in a position that conflicts with existing highway infrastructure, specifically a bus stop directly fronting the site. Its installation would result in unacceptable impacts on pedestrian safety and public transport operations, and is therefore considered inappropriate. The proposal fails to demonstrate a safe and deliverable access arrangement.National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies T2 and T4 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies DMT1 and DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposed development fails to demonstrate that additional demand for parking from the development could be adequately accommodated in the surrounding area. The proposal is therefore likely to add unacceptably to parking stress and congestion in the vicinity of the application site.  As such, it fails to comply with the following policies which seek to ensure proposals show how car parking will be designed and managed and to take into consideration on-street parking availability and existing and planned public transport provision: National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024) Policies T1, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies DMT1 and DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)
description: Change of use of the dwelling (C3) to a children's care home (C2) for up to two children aged 7-18 including the construction of a single storey rear extension
